claims.text: 2024 AAO PPP: indiscriminate use of topical antibiotics or corticosteroids should be avoided
claims.quote: Indiscriminate use of topical antibiotics or corticosteroids should be avoided.

claims.text: viral conjunctivitis will not respond to antibacterial agents
claims.quote: Viral conjunctivitis will not respond to antibacterial agents,

claims.text: mild bacterial conjunctivitis is likely to be self-limited
claims.quote: mild bacterial conjunctivitis is likely to be self-limited

claims.text: no topical antibiotic has been shown superior to another
claims.quote: No evidence exists demonstrating the superiority of any topical antibiotic agent.

claims.text: corticosteroids can prolong adenoviral infections and worsen HSV infections
claims.quote: corticosteroids can potentially prolong adenoviral infections and worsen HSV infections

claims.text: adenoviral conjunctivitis self-limited, improving within 5 to 14 days
claims.quote: Self-limited, with improvement of symptoms and signs within 5 to 14 days

claims.text: adenovirus can remain infectious in a dried state on surfaces for up to 28 days
claims.quote: as the virus can remain infectious in a desiccated state on surfaces for up to 28 days.

claims.text: hyperacute (gonococcal) conjunctivitis needs immediate treatment
claims.quote: Gonococcal conjunctivitis is a hyperacute, vision-threatening infectious condition that requires immediate systemic therapy.

references.cited_as: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Clinical Overview of Pink Eye (Conjunctivitis). Updated April 15, 2024.
references.notes: Page does not state adenovirus surface survival, antibiotic resistance, HSV drug names/referral, or that pharyngoconjunctival fever is frequent in children; those attributions were removed.

claims.text: pharyngoconjunctival fever: conjunctivitis with fever and sore throat, adenovirus serotypes 3, 4, and 7
claims.quote: a syndrome that can produce conjunctivitis as well as a fever and sore throat ... is most commonly caused by infection with adenovirus serotypes 3, 4, and 7.

claims.text: EKC: more severe, serotypes 8, 19, 37, inflames conjunctiva and cornea, can cause vision loss
claims.quote: commonly caused by infection with adenovirus serotypes 8, 19, and 37. EKC causes severe inflammation of the conjunctiva and cornea and can result in vision loss.

claims.text: other viral causes: enterovirus 70, coxsackievirus A24, HSV, VZV
claims.quote: Picornaviruses, such as coxsackievirus A24 and enterovirus 70 ... Herpesviruses, including Herpes simplex virus Varicella-zoster virus

claims.text: most acute infectious conjunctivitis in adults is viral, self-limited, and does not require antimicrobials
claims.quote: Most cases of acute, infectious conjunctivitis in adults are viral and self-limited; these cases do not require antimicrobial treatment.

claims.text: contact lens wearers at higher risk for bacterial keratitis
claims.quote: Contact lens wearers with bacterial conjunctivitis are at higher risk of bacterial keratitis.

claims.text: hygiene: handwashing, separate towels, avoid close contact
claims.quote: washing hands frequently, using separate towels, and avoiding close contact with others

claims.text: stay home with systemic signs of illness, especially if close contact cannot be avoided; return with clinician approval after indicated therapy
claims.quote: Advise patients to remain home if they have viral or bacterial conjunctivitis with systemic signs of illness, especially if they cannot avoid close contact with others. Patients may return to work or school if they receive clinician approval

claims.text: infected students should not attend school if they cannot avoid close contact
claims.quote: Infected students should not attend school if they cannot avoid close contact with others.

claims.text: HSV or VZV lesions may need antiviral treatment
claims.quote: Antiviral medication may be used to treat more serious forms of conjunctivitis.

references.cited_as: Azari AA, Barney NP. Conjunctivitis: A Systematic Review of Diagnosis and Treatment. JAMA. 2013;310(16):1721-1729.
references.record_title: Conjunctivitis: a systematic review of diagnosis and treatment.
references.retrieved_with: PubMed get_article_metadata and get_full_text_article (PMC4049531); Scite verify_papers
references.notes: Full text read via PubMed connector; tables were not in the extracted text, and the PMC web page showed a bot check (not worked around), so no table content is cited. Fluoroquinolone/Pseudomonas claim removed (not in text).

claims.text: acute conjunctivitis affects about 6 million people a year in the US
claims.quote: It is estimated that acute conjunctivitis affects 6 million people annually in the United States.

claims.text: about 1% of primary care office visits related to conjunctivitis
claims.quote: Approximately 1% of all primary care office visits in the United States are related to conjunctivitis.

claims.text: cost of bacterial conjunctivitis $377 million to $857 million per year
claims.quote: The cost of treating bacterial conjunctivitis alone was estimated to be $377 million to $857 million per year.

claims.text: allergic conjunctivitis up to 40% of US population, about 10% seek care
claims.quote: affects up to 40% of the population in the United States; only about 10% of individuals with allergic conjunctivitis seek medical attention

claims.text: seasonal allergic conjunctivitis is 90% of allergic cases in the US
claims.quote: Seasonal allergic conjunctivitis comprises 90% of all allergic conjunctivitis in the United States.

claims.text: gonococcal hyperacute conjunctivitis: copious purulent discharge, high risk of corneal involvement and perforation
claims.quote: Hyperacute bacterial conjunctivitis presents with a severe copious purulent discharge and decreased vision ... carries a high risk for corneal involvement and subsequent corneal perforation.

claims.text: contact lens wearers: high bacterial keratitis risk, remove lenses, treat with topical antibiotics and refer
claims.quote: The possibility of bacterial keratitis is high in contact lens wearers, who should be treated with topical antibiotics and referred to an ophthalmologist. A patient wearing contact lenses should be asked to immediately remove them.

claims.text: prompt referral for visual loss, moderate or severe pain, severe purulent discharge, corneal involvement, history of HSV eye disease (AAO criteria)
claims.quote: should be referred promptly to an ophthalmologist if any of the following develops: visual loss, moderate or severe pain, severe purulent discharge, corneal involvement, ... or history of herpes simplex virus eye disease.

claims.text: lymphadenopathy in up to 50% of viral cases, more common than in bacterial
claims.quote: Lymphadenopathy is observed in up to 50% of viral conjunctivitis cases and is more prevalent in viral conjunctivitis compared with bacterial conjunctivitis.

claims.text: rapid adenovirus antigen test: 89% sensitivity, up to 94% specificity, can prevent unnecessary antibiotics
claims.quote: In-office rapid antigen testing is available for adenoviruses and has 89% sensitivity and up to 94% specificity. This test can identify the viral causes of conjunctivitis and prevent unnecessary antibiotic use.

claims.text: topical antibiotics in viral conjunctivitis: no protection against secondary infection, allergy/toxicity, resistance concern
claims.quote: Topical antibiotics do not protect against secondary infections, and their use may complicate the clinical presentation by causing allergy and toxicity ... Increased resistance is also of concern with frequent use of antibiotics.

claims.text: antibiotic choice depends on availability, allergies, resistance patterns, cost
claims.quote: Factors that influence antibiotic choice are local availability, patient allergies, resistance pat terns, and cost.

claims.text: steroids prolong viral conjunctivitis and can worsen undiagnosed ulcers, leading to corneal melt and blindness
claims.quote: the refore prolonging the course of viral conjunctivitis. In addition, if an undiagnosed corneal ulcer secondary to herpes, bacteria, or fungus is present, steroids can worsen the condition, leading to corneal melt and blindness.

claims.text: antihistamines and mast cell stabilizers superior to placebo for allergic conjunctivitis
claims.quote: In a large systemic review, both antihistamines and mast cell stabilizers were superior to placebo in reducing the symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis

claims.text: contagious period: adenovirus about 10 to 14 days, bacterial about 2 to 7 days
claims.quote: Incubation and communicability are estimated to be 5 to 12 days and 10 to 14 days, respectively. ... The period of incubation and communicability is estimated to be 1 to 7 days and 2 to 7 days, respectively.

claims.text: topical antibiotics allow earlier return to school or work
claims.quote: Topical antibiotics decrease the duration of bacterial conjunctivitis and allow earlier return to school or work.

claims.text: antibiotics should be considered for purulent/mucopurulent conjunctivitis, distinct discomfort, contact lens wearers, immunocompromised, suspected chlamydial or gonococcal
claims.quote: Antibiotic therapy should be considered in cases of purulent or mucopurulent conjunctivitis and for patients who have distinct discomfort, who wear contact lenses, who are immunocompromised, and who have suspected chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis.

claims.text: herpes: vesicular eyelid lesions, antivirals recommended
claims.quote: accompanying vesicular eyelid lesions may be present. Topical and oral antivirals are recommended

claims.text: about 80% of infectious conjunctivitis is viral
claims.quote: The most common cause of infectious conjunctivitis is viral infection (~80% of cases), followed by bacterial.

claims.text: clinical accuracy for viral conjunctivitis may be under 50%
claims.quote: the rate of clinical accuracy in diagnosing viral conjunctivitis may be <50%

claims.text: review advises delaying antibiotic prescriptions until bacterial cause confirmed
claims.quote: Prescription of antibiotics should be delayed until a bacterial etiology is confirmed

claims.text: adenoviruses cause 65-90% of viral conjunctivitis
claims.quote: Adenoviruses are the cause of most (65–90%) cases of viral conjunctivitis

claims.text: HSV: topical and/or oral antivirals recommended; topical corticosteroids avoided
claims.quote: Topical and/or oral antivirals are recommended to shorten the duration of illness.,Because topical corticosteroids can potentiate HSV,,they should be avoided

claims.text: about 32% of acute infectious conjunctivitis bacterial in adult GP sample; 50-75% in children
claims.quote: Approximately 32% of acute infectious conjunctivitis cases are caused by bacteria ... In children, the bacterial disease is responsible for 50–75% of conjunctivitis cases

claims.text: hyperacute bacterial conjunctivitis needs immediate management to prevent corneal involvement and perforation
claims.quote: warrants immediate ophthalmic management to prevent corneal involvement and potentially perforation.

claims.text: chlamydia causes 1.8-5.6% of acute conjunctivitis, often with concurrent genital infection
claims.quote: Chlamydia is the cause of 1.8–5.6% of all acute conjunctivitis cases.Chlamydial conjunctivitis primarily has a unilateral presentation with concurrent genital infection

claims.text: school policies and work pressure may influence prescribing
claims.quote: Social factors, such as school policies or pressure to reduce absence from work, may also influence general practitioners to prescribe topical antibiotics.

claims.text: cultures used in neonates and considered for immunocompromised, hyperacute, recurrent, severe or chronic purulent cases
claims.quote: Routine bacteriologic examinations are neither typically performed nor practical ... except in neonates.Culturing should also be considered for immunocompromised patients or for patients with hyperacute cases

claims.text: follicular reaction mainly infectious; papillary mainly allergic
claims.quote: follicular, mainly infectious; papillary, mainly allergic

claims.text: glued eyelids, lack of itching suggest bacterial
claims.quote: Bacterial conjunctivitis is strongly suggested by glued eyelids, lack of itching, and lack of history of conjunctivitis.

claims.text: preauricular node more common in viral than bacterial
claims.quote: Lymphadenopathy, such as an enlarged, tender preauricular lymph node, is more common in viral versus bacterial conjunctivitis.

claims.text: HSV branching lesions; subepithelial infiltrates within 7-10 days of EKC onset
claims.quote: HSV infection typically appears as branching lesions with intensely stained end bulbs ... Multifocal subepithelial infiltrates may develop in the cornea within 7–10 days after the onset of clinical signs of infection.

claims.text: viral tests not routine in primary care; AdenoPlus sensitivity 39.5-93%
claims.quote: Viral diagnostic tests are not used routinely in a primary care setting ... Observed sensitivity of the test ranges from 39.5 to 93%.

claims.text: no medications approved for adenoviral conjunctivitis; supportive treatment
claims.quote: As no medications are currently approved for adenoviral conjunctivitis, treatment is mainly supportive (cold compresses, chilled artificial tears)

claims.text: adenovirus relatively resistant to disinfection
claims.quote: Adenoviruses are nonenveloped viruses that are relatively resistant to disinfection.

claims.text: pain or photophobia can signal bacterial keratitis, anterior uveitis, acute angle-closure glaucoma
claims.quote: pain or photophobia, which can be signs of bacterial keratitis, anterior uveitis, or acute angle-closure glaucoma.

claims.text: immediate referral for visual loss, moderate to severe pain, severe purulent discharge, corneal involvement
claims.quote: Referral to an ophthalmologist or eye care professional should be performed immediately for cases that involve visual loss, moderate to severe pain, severe purulent discharge, or any corneal involvement.

references.cited_as: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). How to Treat Pink Eye. Updated April 15, 2024.
references.notes: Page lists topical antihistamine and vasoconstrictor drops, not mast cell stabilizers or named products, so the allergic-drops sentence is now cited to ref 3. It does not address adenovirus antivirals (now cited to ref 4).

claims.text: antibiotics will not help viral pink eye
claims.quote: Antibiotics will NOT improve viral pink eye; these drugs are not effective against viruses.

claims.text: viral usually clears in 7 to 14 days; some cases 2 to 3 weeks or more
claims.quote: It usually clears up in 7 to 14 days without treatment and without any long-term consequences. ... in some cases, viral conjunctivitis can take 2 to 3 weeks or more to clear up.

claims.text: mild bacterial often clears in 2 to 5 days without treatment; up to 2 weeks
claims.quote: It usually clears up in 2 to 5 days without treatment but can take 2 weeks to go away completely.

claims.text: antibiotics may shorten infection, reduce complications, prevent spread
claims.quote: Antibiotics may help shorten the length of infection, reduce complications, and prevent the spread to others.

claims.text: cold compresses and artificial tears for relief
claims.quote: Use cold compresses and artificial tears to help relieve some of the inflammation and dryness caused by pink eye.

claims.text: see a provider: eye pain, light sensitivity, blurred vision not improving when discharge wiped, weakened immune system
claims.quote: Eye pain ... Light sensitivity ... Blurred vision that does not improve when discharge is wiped from the eyes ... A weakened immune system

claims.text: see a provider if bacterial pink eye does not improve after 24 hours of antibiotics
claims.quote: If you have bacterial pink eye which does not improve after 24 hours of antibiotic use

claims.text: allergic pink eye usually improves when allergen removed
claims.quote: usually improves by removing the allergen from the person's environment.

claims.quote: 1 of every 5 antibiotic users filled prescriptions for antibiotic-corticosteroids, which are contraindicated for acute conjunctivitis.

claims.text: wash hands at least 20 seconds; before and after drops/ointment
claims.quote: Wash your hands often with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. ... Wash your hands before and after cleaning, or applying eye drops or ointment to your infected eye.

claims.text: avoid touching or rubbing eyes
claims.quote: Avoid touching or rubbing your eyes with your fingers.

claims.text: do not share pillows, washcloths, towels, eye drops, makeup, brushes
claims.quote: Do not share personal items, like pillows, washcloths, towels, eye drops, eye or face makeup, makeup brushes,

claims.text: wash linens in hot water; clean eyeglasses
claims.quote: Wash pillowcases, sheets, washcloths, and towels often in hot water and detergent. ... Clean eyeglasses, being careful not to contaminate shared items like hand towels.

claims.text: stop wearing contacts; discard disposable lenses and cases
claims.quote: Stop wearing contact lenses until you no longer have symptoms ... including disposable contact lenses and cases.

claims.text: do not use swimming pools
claims.quote: Do not use swimming pools.
